quotes.quote:
mailing address, contact name and phone number, number of years doing business 
with, and type of work performed.  Personal references cannot be considered.

Therefore, all instructions contained in this RFP

findings.title: Contract Term and Annual Appropriation Requirement
findings.fact: The contract term is one year (July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028), contingent on appropriation. Continued funding is subject to annual statutory process and appropriation.
findings.business_implication: The contract is not guaranteed beyond the initial term; funding for subsequent years depends on annual appropriations and a new RFP process.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a one-year contract with potential for continuation; budget accordingly and prepare for annual renewal processes.

findings.title: Subscription License Costs Only Upon Utilization
findings.fact: As a Service subscription license costs shall be incurred at the individual license level only as the individual license is utilized within a fully functioning solution. Subscription costs will not be applicable during implementation and solution development prior to full acceptance.

findings.action_recommendation: Structure pricing model to align with utilization-based billing; ensure contract clearly defines acceptance criteria.

quotes.quote: As a Service subscription license costs shall be incurred at the individual license level only as the individual license is utilized within a fully functioning solution. findings.title: Additional License Requests Limited to 5%

findings.business_implication: The vendor cannot oversell licenses beyond 5% of actual utilization; this limits revenue potential and requires accurate forecasting.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure license count estimates are accurate; plan for potential budget review constraints.

quotes.quote: Additional subscription license requests above actual utilization may not exceed 5% of the total and are subject to Delaware budget and technical review.

findings.title: Contract Execution Within 20 Days
findings.fact: The successful vendor shall promptly execute a contract incorporating the terms of this RFP within twenty (20) days after award of the contract.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must be prepared to finalize contract quickly after award; delays could result in annulment of award.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare contract review and execution processes in advance to meet the 20-day deadline.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor shall promptly execute a contract incorporating the terms of this RFP within twenty (20) days after award of the contract.

findings.title: No Work Before Purchase Order

findings.business_implication: The vendor cannot start work until a formal purchase order is received; this may delay project initiation.
findings.action_recommendation: Coordinate with the State to ensure timely issuance of purchase order; plan project start date accordingly.

quotes.quote: No vendor is to begin any service prior to receipt of a State of Delaware purchase order signed by two authorized representatives of the agency requesting service, properly processed through the State of Delaware Accounting Office and the Department of Finance.

findings.title: Award Annulment for Failure to Execute
findings.fact: If the vendor to whom the award is made fails to enter into the agreement as herein provided, the award will be annulled, and an award may be made to another vendor.
findings.business_implication: Failure to execute the contract within the specified timeframe can result in loss of the award.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all internal approvals are obtained promptly to avoid annulment.

quotes.quote: If the vendor to whom the award is made fails to enter into the agreement as herein provided, the award will be annulled, and an award may be made to another vendor.

findings.title: State Option to Extend Contract
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to extend this contract on a month-to-month basis for a period of up to three months after the term of the full contract has been completed.
findings.business_implication: The State may extend the contract up to three months beyond the initial term, potentially affecting resource planning.
findings.action_recommendation: Be prepared for possible extension; include terms for month-to-month extension in pricing and capacity planning.

quotes.quote: The State reserves the right to extend this contract on a month-to-month basis for a period of up to three months after the term of the full contract has been completed.

findings.title: Vendors Not Restricted from Lower Pricing
findings.fact: Vendors are not restricted from offering lower pricing at any time during the contract term.
findings.business_implication: The vendor can reduce prices during the contract, which may be beneficial for competitiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Consider pricing flexibility as a strategic option.

quotes.quote: Vendors are not restricted from offering lower pricing at any time during the contract term.

findings.title: Prohibition on Collusion and Fraud
findings.fact: Any evidence of agreement or collusion among vendors to restrain competition will render offers void. By responding, vendor warrants no collusion and no participation in RFP development.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must ensure its proposal is independent and not coordinated with competitors; any violation could void the proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure internal processes prevent any appearance of collusion; document independence.

findings.title: Prohibition on Lobbying and Gratuities
findings.fact: Lobbying or providing gratuities to State employees concerning the RFP is strictly prohibited. Violations result in immediate rejection and barring from further participation.
findings.business_implication: Any attempt to influence State employees through lobbying or gratuities will disqualify the vendor.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all communications with State personnel follow the RFP's specified channels; avoid any gifts or lobbying activities.

quotes.quote: Lobbying or providing gratuities shall be strictly prohibited. findings.title: Warranty Against Contingent Fees
findings.fact: The selected vendor warrants that no person or selling agency has been employed to solicit or secure the contract for a commission or contingent fee. Breach allows the State to annul the contract or recover the full amount of such fee.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must ensure no third-party contingency fees are involved; violation could lead to contract annulment and financial penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Review any third-party agreements to ensure compliance with this warranty.

quotes.quote: The selected vendor will warrant that no person or selling agency has been employed or retained to solicit or secure a contract resulting from this RFP upon agreement or understanding for a commission, or a percentage, brokerage or contingent fee. For breach or violation of this warranty, the State of Delaware shall have the right to annul any contract resulting from this RFP without liability or at its discretion deduct from the contract price or otherwise recover the full amount of such commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee.

findings.title: Restriction on Soliciting State Employees
findings.fact: Until contract award, vendors shall not directly or indirectly solicit any State employee to leave State employment without prior written approval. Violation may result in rejection of the proposal.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must avoid recruiting State employees during the bidding process; violation could disqualify the proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Instruct HR and recruitment teams to avoid soliciting State employees until after award.

quotes.quote: Until contract award, vendors shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit any employee of the State of Delaware to leave the State of Delaware’s employ in order to accept employment with the vendor, its affiliates, actual or prospective contractors, or any person acting in concert with vendor, without prior written approval of the State of Delaware’s contracting officer. Solicitation of State of Delaware employees by a vendor may result in rejection of the vendor’s proposal.

findings.title: Independent Contractor Relationship
findings.fact: The parties shall be independent contractors; nothing creates an agency, partnership, joint venture, or employment relationship. Each party is responsible for its own compliance with employment-related laws.
findings.business_implication: The vendor is not an employee of the State and is responsible for its own taxes, insurance, and compliance; the State is not liable for vendor's obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure proper classification of personnel and compliance with all applicable laws.

quotes.quote: The parties to the contract shall be independent contractors to one another, and nothing herein shall be deemed to cause this agreement to create an agency, partnership, joint venture or employment relationship between parties. Each party shall be responsible for compliance with all applicable workers compensation, unemployment, disability insurance, social security withholding and all other similar matters.

findings.title: State Discretion on Work Location

findings.business_implication: The State can dictate where work is performed, potentially affecting vendor's operational costs and logistics.

findings.fact: The vendor must be properly licensed and authorized to transact business in Delaware as provided in 30 Del. C. § 2101, and must furnish proof of licensure or initiate the application process prior to award.

findings.title: Compliance with State Health Mandates
findings.fact: Awarded vendors with employees working at State facilities must comply with any health mandate or policy issued by the State related to a pandemic or State of Emergency, including those applying to State employees.
